newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand stooped to close around six-month lows against the dollar on Monday with Reserve Bank intervention keeping the scene from looking a lot worse.

"This morning we saw some local (dollar) buying and it went up and tested 4.5750 for the first time. It then drifted back down to 4.5700 and that's when we started seeing investment houses based in London have a go."
"It range-traded after that because the Reserve Bank was on the upside," said one forex dealer.
The rand was last quoted at 4.5715/5745 against the dollar from 4.5620/5650 late Friday but slightly up from earlier six-month low of 4.5740 bid.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank made its presence felt early, selling $100 million around 4.5750 to indicate the barrier for the day.
They said in the absence of major market moving news on Tuesday, the rand was likely keep to a range of 4.5750-5675.
In cross rate action, the local unit was changing hands at 7.6481/6577 on sterling from 7.6326/6399 late Friday.
It was also pegged at 0.3922/3927 on mark from Friday's 0.3939/3942. Against the Japanese yen, the rand was at 25.2662/3046 from 25.3721/3997.
In the bond market, the key R150 yield jumped early to 14.435 percent, which became the bellwhether's ceiling for the rest of the session.
The jobbers who had sold off over the morning quickly ran out of steam and not content to stay short overnight, scratched for stock toward the close.
The R150 finished at 14.37 percent, a tad stronger than Friday's late level of 14.375 percent.

"I think there might be a little correction effort happening here with some of the offshore fund managers getting a bit nervous about emerging markets. Not sure how long it will last though," said one dealer.
The Bond Exchange earlier said foreigners sold a hefty net 1.9 billion rands' worth of South African bonds last week.
The long bond was seen capped for the time being at 14.425 percent -- its 30-day moving average -- with downside limited to 14.35 percent.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage eased to 9.592 billion rand on Saturday from 9.606 billion rand on Friday.
Friday's Bond Exchange turnover was 8.5 billion from 44.75 billion rand on Thursday which was a settlement day.
